layer_time.rule: t = layer area x 0.2 mm / 8 mm3/s x 1.08 (BL-053)
layer_time.method: park-and-dwell: the coupon job's printer preset gets a per-layer dwell in 'Layer change G-code' (park the nozzle clear of the parts, G4 S<dwell>), so each layer is printed at the frame profile's own speed and then cools with the nozzle away, as a frame interface does while the nozzle works elsewhere on the part; a 15 x 15 mm prime pillar beside the parts takes the ooze after each dwell. Not the slicer slow-down: it keeps the hot nozzle over the small coupon for the whole layer (Vaes 2021: slower printing did not lengthen the cooling that sets the weld) and it stops at 'Min print speed'. Dummy towers only as the fallback if the dwell oozes.
layer_time.why_time_not_volume: The weld between layers is set by the interface temperature history (Seppala 2017; Vaes 2021): the time the layer below cools before the next road lands, with the nozzle away. A tower only buys that time; its volume does nothing else, so a dwell with the nozzle parked gives the same history without the filament.

sources.weld: Seppala, Han, Hillgartner, Davis, Migler, 'Weld formation during material extrusion additive manufacturing', Soft Matter 13 (2017) 6761-6769, doi:10.1039/C7SM00950J (NIST): the interface temperature history (time above Tg, via the rheological shift factor) sets interdiffusion and the weld strength
sources.speed: Vaes, Coppens, Goderis, Zoetelief, Van Puyvelde, 'The extent of interlayer bond strength during fused filament fabrication of nylon copolymers', Polymers 13 (2021) 2677, doi:10.3390/polym13162677: weld time from the measured thermal history predicts the PA bond; halving the print speed (11 -> 5.5 mm/s) doubled the build time but gave no clear change in weld time or bond strength
sources.slowdown: Bambu Lab wiki 'auto cooling' (https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/software/bambu-studio/auto-cooling) and OrcaSlicer wiki 'Material cooling' (https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/material_settings/cooling/material_cooling): 'Slow printing down for better layer cooling' lowers the print speed until the layer takes the 'Layer time' threshold, never below 'Min print speed'; forum request 'Park hotend for minimum layer time' (https://forum.bambulab.com/t/park-hotend-for-minimum-layer-time/70222): Bambu Studio cannot park the nozzle to make up the time
sources.gcode: OrcaSlicer wiki 'Machine G-code' (https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/printer_settings/machine%20gcode/printer_machine_gcode): the 'Layer change G-code' is inserted at every layer change after the Z lift (same field in Bambu Studio, Printer settings > Machine G-code; forum 'Custom G-code for Pause - Wipe - Resume', https://forum.bambulab.com/t/solved-custom-g-code-for-pause-wipe-resume/40620)

h1_as_is.verdict: H1 as is needs values the coupons cannot plausibly reach (or measure)
h1_as_is.plausibility: A (Z / SBS, booked fatigue ratio 0.30 and XY): NOT reachable at any Z / SBS: static_fatigue saturates at 0.766, R1 saturates at 0.585, joint_fatigue saturates at 0.702, lug_fatigue saturates at 1.02 (the in-plane terms govern once the layers are strong). B (fatigue ratio credited to every term, in-plane too): ratio >= 0.52 with Z >= 36.8 and SBS >= 21.3 MPa; cited PA12-CF ratios are 0.25-0.32 x UTS (Siebert et al., Proc. TU Sofia 76(3) 2025, FFF PA12-CF15, 1e6 cycles) and 0.40 at best (Stratasys FDM Nylon 12CF white paper, run-outs at 1e6; docs/research/frame_comp_A.md), and CA-1-PAHT tests the shear term only, so the in-plane ratio would need its own coupon. C (all allowables x 2.079): XY >= 89.7, Z >= 40.9, SBS >= 23.6 MPa hot/wet B-basis, against a dry TDS XY mean of 88 (V2.0) / 92 (V3.0) MPa and a kindest cited hot/wet Z B-basis of 37.9 MPa (typical 23.1). Verdict: H1 as is needs values the coupons cannot plausibly reach (or measure).

assumptions.text: The Bambu TDS +/- values are standard deviations of an ISO 527 set of n 5 (the ISO 527-1 minimum; the TDS gives no n): B-basis k 3.4066 on the lower published mean of each property.
Wet / dry = 0.82 XY (Bambu's 12-18 % decline, the 18 % floor; the XY bending pair reads 0.92) and 0.80 Z (the Z bending pair 49 / 61): bending pairs stand in for tensile.
40 C / 23 C = 0.82 from the Fiberlogy PA12 CF15 UTS curve (Ciganas 2026), the lowest of the direct and two Tg-shift readings; a PA12-CF15 grade stands in for PAHT-CF.
Interlayer shear allowable = Z / sqrt 3 (von Mises), was 0.6 x Z with no source; the frame code's 0.6 x s_z rule is fed s_z = tau / 0.6, so the layer-normal term reads 3.8 % harsh.
Hot/wet modulus = 0.716 (Ciganas E 40 / 23 C) x 0.82 (wet strength ratio) = 0.587; buckling rows are scaled by 0.587 / 0.6 from the booked basis.
PAHT fatigue at 1e5 = 0.30 x the hot/wet B-basis static strength (record ratio, unchanged).
The bound on any local fix removes the hot-spot regions from the utilisation population and assumes nothing else changes (a real doubler also attracts load: the bound is optimistic for it).
assumptions.settled_by: not needed: the bound already fails

assumptions.text: Each 304 sleeve is cut to the measured boss depth + 0.05-0.15 mm, so the 0.6 N m preload sits on the steel and the PAHT under the plates sees only the hip tipping load (BL-055 model, FLANGE-RIGID).
assumptions.settled_by: HB-6b-SLV (no plate witness mark before load, paint marks after T5)

assumptions.text: 304 tube 1/4 in OD x 0.010 in wall (ID 5.84 mm) is bought as cold-drawn tube; the check uses the annealed record yield 215 MPa (sleeve SF 1.22 at the K 0.14 preload).
The cap covers PAHT filament + the fasteners / metal parts that join or clamp the printed body; crown, pins, bushings and the SLM Ti hip mount carry over and are outside it.

BL-079 (replaces LAYER-TIME): the coupon jobs hold every layer >= the slowest frame half's median layer time at the real 0.20 mm profile with a per-layer park-and-dwell in 'Layer change G-code' (normal print speed, then the nozzle parked clear for the dwell); matching the cooling time, not the tower volume, is what matches the interlayer weld (Seppala 2017, Vaes 2021). The slicer slow-down is not used: it keeps the nozzle on the part and stops at the minimum speed.
assumptions.settled_by: slicer preview (layer-time view) and the job's logged shortest layer time

assumptions.text: BL-079 thresholds for H1 as is hold the in-plane (XY) allowable at the booked hot/wet B-basis 43.14 MPa: no coupon here measures the XY tensile B-basis (CA-4-PAHT flexural strength is for the record).
assumptions.settled_by: not settled by these coupons (a later XY coupon if H1 as is comes within reach)

assumptions.text: BL-079: the fatigue ratio measured in shear (CA-1-PAHT) is booked to every term of the layer rule (the record's single ratio 0.30); the thresholds are given at the booked 0.30, so a better measured ratio is not credited to the in-plane term.
The A2 M5 x 45 DIN 7984 costs the same as the cited A2 M5 x 35 (Zoro 50-pack); the Ti lines are the kit's USD 2.50 shop-price ASSUMPTION.
One 10 ml threadlocker bottle covers about 10 frames (per-frame share USD 0.90).
Coupon jobs use 1.3 x the coupon volume (brim, ties, purge).
